sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
The core gameplay of Drop Dunks revolves around guiding falling balls through a hoop. The game features simple controls, allowing you to use your mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to play. You'll need to time your movements perfectly to catch the balls as they fall from the top of the screen. The game's physics engine makes the balls behave realistically, taking into account factors like gravity and bounce. This adds a layer of unpredictability to the game, making it more challenging and engaging.

One of the key mechanics in Drop Dunks is the ability to chain reactions. By catching multiple balls in a single move, you'll earn bonus points and increase your score multiplier. This makes it essential to think strategically and plan your moves ahead. As you progress through levels, the game introduces new obstacles and power-ups that can either hinder or help your progress. For example, you might encounter a ball that's stuck in a corner or a power-up that gives you a temporary speed boost.

The game also features a variety of balls with different properties. Some balls are bigger or smaller than others, affecting their speed and bounciness. Others might have a higher or lower score value, giving you a reason to prioritize certain balls over others. Understanding the properties of each ball is crucial to achieving high scores and advancing through levels.
